body: Macau is a Special Administrative Region of China, so for country streaks purposes, it is counted as China.

Coverage in Macau is limited to Generation 2, which results in lower camera quality, a circular blur, and colors that appear washed out and overexposed. This distinctive look can be a key identifier for Macau.
Macau uses black licence plates with white text. The plates can be either long or square.
Cylindrical grey lamp posts with a black painted bottom are common in Macau. This distinguishes them from similar lamp posts in Hong Kong, which do not have the black painted bottom.
Due to Macau's history as a Portuguese colony, the Portuguese language is commonly seen on storefronts and signs, alongside Chinese.
The unique white street signs with a blue border around the Chinese and Portuguese text are a distinctive feature of Macau.
Gambling is a major industry in Macau, so you will see many extravagant and kitschy casinos. Because of the old Generation 2 coverage, many newer casinos may appear to be under construction.
The northern part of Macau is characterized by dense apartment buildings, narrow gridded streets, and cars parked on both sides.
In the south of Macau, you can find a hilly, rural region with narrow, winding roads. The washed-out early Generation 2 coverage can be a key clue for identification in this less-cluttered area.
The Sai Van Bridge can be identified by its unique cuboid towers with arches in them.
The Amizade Bridge is recognizable by its distinctive red guardrails.
